subject: April invoice: unexpected overage and VAT treatment
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena@orthosys.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orthosys.com
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 09:12:00 +02:00
Subject: April invoice spike — need clarity on metering and VAT

Hi Michael,

Hope you're well. We just received the April invoice (attached) and there is a substantial overage line (~€18,200) that we didn't expect. Our engineering team ran a quick check and pointed to a steady stream of calls to the /streaming/generate endpoint during the 04/12–04/14 window. We did not run any heavy batch jobs in production during that time.

Two quick asks:
- Can you share a per-endpoint usage export (token-level) for 2027-04-01 to 2027-04-30 so we can map requests to our internal logs?
- How will VAT be applied if this overage is disputed / credited? Procurement has placed a temporary hold until we reconcile.

We really appreciate a fast turnaround on this — finance needs to close the month.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Finance — OrthoSys
Elena.Rossi@orthosys.com
Attachment: invoice_202704.pdf (PDF, 142KB)
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@orthosys.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 11:05:00 +02:00
Subject: Fwd: April invoice spike — need clarity on metering and VAT

Ben / Kim / Priyom — looping you in to triage.

Elena reports a ~€18k unexpected overage in April tied to streaming traffic over 04/12–04/14. She asked for token-level export and VAT implications. Please:
1) Confirm whether any of OrthoSys's keys were flagged for staging/dev traffic or if there was a routing fallback to a higher-rate model variant during that window.
2) Export a per-endpoint token usage CSV for 2027-04-01..04-30 and highlight high-volume sessions.
3) Recommend remediation/credit options and the VAT handling approach for any one-time credit we might grant (EU reverse-charge vs invoice adjustment).

Elena — we will get you the export and a recommended remediation plan today or tomorrow EOD.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.ai | +1 415 555 0199
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Rossi <elena@orthosys.com>
Date: Fri, 7 May 2027 15:20:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: April invoice spike — initial triage

On Fri, May 7, 2027 at 11:05 AM Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Ben / Kim / Priyom — looping you in to triage.

Quick update from ops / metering: attached is the filtered usage_export_202704_filtered.csv focusing on high-volume sessions. Top-line findings:
- There are ~1.2M tokens attributed to a continuous streaming session from key AK-ORT-01 between 2027-04-12 02:40 UTC and 2027-04-14 18:10 UTC.
- That API key had been used from an IP range that matches OrthoSys but we also see a short-lived spike of requests from 35.200.14.9 (likely an automated test agent).
- A routing fallback occurred on 2027-04-12 02:41 UTC when the primary low-cost variant was saturated; requests were routed to an auxiliary variant with the platform's capped-rate multiplier enabled. That multiplier increases per-token billable units for streaming sessions over 1M tokens in a 24h window.

Preliminary cause: continuous streaming + routing fallback + capped-rate multiplier = unexpectedly high billable tokens. No evidence of a Redwood pricing miscompute; the multiplier was applied according to our ratecard policy.

Next steps proposed:
- Share the attached CSV with OrthoSys for correlation with their logs (attached).
- Offer a one-time goodwill credit while they validate whether the test agent was internal. I suggest a 30% credit of the disputed overage amount pending confirmation.
- For VAT: if we issue a credit (invoice adjustment), we can produce a credit memo and updated VAT calculation; if they prefer a cash refund, tax treatment depends on their EU entity and the original invoice VAT lines (finance can advise).

Attachments: usage_export_202704_filtered.csv (CSV, 1.1MB)

Ben Carter
Billing Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai
From: Elena Rossi <elena@orthosys.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@orthosys.com
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 08:45:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: April invoice spike — need clarity on metering and VAT

Thanks for the quick triage. A couple of clarifying points from our side:
- The IP Ben flagged (35.200.14.9) belongs to an external vendor that ran a data migration test without telling us — we are confirming with them. If that test is the source we will accept responsibility for the requests.
- For timeline: procurement needs a firm proposal by EOD Monday or they will hold the payment.

Two asks:
1) If we accept responsibility for the traffic, can Redwood provide a granular per-session breakout so we can match to vendor logs?
2) If Redwood issues a credit memo (preferred), how long until our VAT liability is adjusted on your side? Will we receive an updated invoice and credit memo we can forward to our tax advisor?

Regards,
Elena
From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@orthosys.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 8 May 2027 10:00:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: April invoice spike — resolution proposal and next steps

Elena — appreciate the fast response and the vendor follow-up.

We can provide a per-session breakout (session id, start/end, tokens, originating IP) — Ben attached the filtered CSV earlier; we will run a further sessionization job and produce a session-level CSV by EOD Monday. That should let you reconcile with the vendor logs.

On credits/VAT: our recommended path to minimize tax friction is to issue a credit memo and an adjusted invoice. Once the credit memo is posted we will regenerate VAT lines on our side and provide both documents (credit memo + revised invoice) within 3 business days of agreement. If you prefer a refund instead we will work with finance on the tax implication, but that typically takes longer to reflect in tax filings.

Proposed commercial path:
- One-time goodwill credit equal to 30% of the disputed overage (€5,460) while you validate vendor responsibility.
- If OrthoSys confirms vendor-caused traffic, we revert to standard billing and you cover the remaining disputed amount; if Redwood finds a billing error on our end, we will issue a full adjustment.

I've attached a short proposed credit term doc so procurement can sign off quickly (proposed_credit_term.docx). If that works, I'll open a HubSpot ticket and a DocuSign agreement for the credit memo.

Links: HubSpot deal and ticket are in the related links.

Thanks,
Michael Grant
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
Attachment: proposed_credit_term.docx (DOCX, 18KB)
